topics.topic: Allowed api_base_url components and exact path-joining normalization
questions: Are user information, query, fragment and an existing base path allowed in `api_base_url`, and does removing a trailing slash remove one slash or all trailing slashes?

Are userinfo, an existing path, query, fragment, percent-encoded host, multiple trailing slashes, IPv6 zone identifiers or other legal URL components allowed, and exactly how many trailing slashes are removed before joining?
Which URL components may `api_base_url` contain, and exactly how is the operation path joined to a permitted base path?

judgement.why: This asks the same unchanged base-URL component and path-joining question judged in P1.

precedent.topic: Allowed api_base_url components and operation-path resolution
precedent.why: The accepted base-URL grammar, joining rules and Host serialization are format and encoding details belonging to State 6.

topics.topic: Encoding or rejection of unsafe multipart port names
questions: How are quotes, backslashes, controls, non-ASCII characters or line breaks in port names escaped or refused when inserted into multipart headers?
How are quotes, backslashes, control characters, non-ASCII text or other header-unsafe characters in port names encoded or refused when inserted into multipart headers?
How are quotes, backslashes, control characters, non-ASCII characters and CR/LF in multipart port names handled?

judgement.why: This asks the same unchanged multipart port-name encoding question judged in P19.

precedent.topic: Exact multipart wire encoding and handling of unsafe multipart port names
precedent.why: Multipart header escaping, media-type grammar, boundary generation and wire framing are format and encoding decisions belonging to State 6 or later.

topics.topic: Ownership, permissions, existence, and creation policy for the data directory and its files
questions: What exact ownership and permission modes satisfy `private`, including directories, the database, WAL files, lock files, value files and spool files?

Which ownership and permission modes count as private for directories and files—must all group/other bits be zero as for the configuration file, and are ACLs, hard links and inherited permissions checked?
What owner, mode and existence checks apply, and may the kernel create a missing data directory or its internal subdirectories?

judgement.why: This asks the same unchanged definition of a private data directory judged in P20.

precedent.topic: Filesystem conditions that define a private data directory
quotes:
The directory and everything in it
   are private to the kernel's user; the kernel refuses to start otherwise.
precedent.why: The exact meaning of private filesystem state was already unspecified in this unchanged passage.

topics.topic: Required completeness and exact port sets for authored trial inputs and expected outputs
questions: Must trial inputs contain exactly every input port and no additional names, and when expected outputs are present must they contain exactly every output port or may they be partial?
Must an authored case supply exactly every input port and, when expectations are present, exactly every output port, or are missing and extra ports or partial expected outputs allowed?
May an authored trial case assert only selected outputs, or must `expected_outputs`, when present, exactly match all contract output ports?

judgement.why: This asks the same trial-case port-completeness question judged in P8.

precedent.topic: Required completeness and exclusivity of authored trial input and output maps
precedent.why: Required and optional request fields and the exact trial-case input and expected-output shapes belong to State 6 schemas.

topics.topic: Required determinism and handling of untrapped nondeterministic sources
questions: Are unlisted clock sources such as `time.clock_gettime`, `time.thread_time`, `os.times`, `resource.getrusage`, or direct `_datetime` access allowed, or must they also be blocked?

Is deterministic output a required sandbox guarantee, despite accessible process/thread scheduling, object addresses, host/runtime observations and other untrapped nondeterminism, or is only the admission algorithm and ordering required to be deterministic?

What prevents or classifies nondeterminism from untrapped process and filesystem observations such as process IDs, object-address representations, directory metadata or ordering, interpreter/runtime metadata and similar standard-library facilities?
What must happen when code uses a nondeterministic source that is not in the closed trap list?

judgement.why: This asks the same unchanged determinism and untrapped-source question judged in P9.

precedent.topic: Required determinism and handling of untrapped nondeterministic observations
quotes: The same implementation on the same input yields the same output digest twice.
precedent.why: The determinism requirement and its enforcement question predated the change and were untouched by it.

topics.topic: Storage model and resolution behavior for revision-addressed manifests
questions: What operation reads a file at a revision: must `manifest_location` be a Git repository, a checked-out immutable directory, or another versioned store, and what happens when the revision cannot be resolved?

How does the kernel obtain a file at the named revision: read from an already checked-out tree, invoke a repository object reader, verify the working tree revision, or interpret `manifest_revision` in some other way?
Is the manifest location a checked-out immutable directory, a Git repository whose object must be read at the named revision, or another revisioned store?

judgement.why: This asks the same manifest-revision retrieval and failure question judged in P3.

precedent.topic: Manifest revision semantics, retrieval mechanism, and failure behavior
quotes:
**The manifest at a revision**: `manifest_location` is a directory inside a
   git repository and `manifest_revision` a commit of it; `bindings` reads
   `<service_id>.json` of that directory at that commit as a git object, never
   from the working tree, so a record changes only with the configured revision
   (A08 rules 1 and 6).

**A manifest that cannot be read at start** in
   `bindings.check_installed_instances`: the start stops and names it; every
   start step is required (State 3, "Start").
precedent.why: The later text defines revision reads as Git-object reads at a commit and makes an unreadable startup manifest stop startup.

topics.topic: Definition of hosts covered by the plain-HTTP loopback exception
questions: Does this mean only a literal loopback IP, also names such as `localhost`, or any hostname that resolves to loopback, and how are unusual IPv4 and IPv6 textual forms classified?
How is the loopback exception determined, including IPv4, IPv6, alternate numeric spellings and DNS names?

judgement.why: This asks the same unchanged plain-HTTP loopback classification question judged in P11.

precedent.topic: Secure determination of the plain-HTTP loopback exception
quotes:
Plain `http` is allowed only for an instance of
   class `local_dev` or `disposable_rig`, as the manifest instance's `class`
   states — an absent or unknown class counts as `production` — or one whose
   `api_base_url` host is a loopback address; any other plain `http` target is refused before sending.
precedent.why: The definition of loopback concerns unchanged text and was not made material by the change.

topics.topic: Empty node IDs and ordering between nodes and flow endpoints
questions: Must `node_id` be non-empty, or how does an actual node whose id is the empty string order against a flow endpoint?
Is an empty `node_id` refused, or how are a real empty-named node and a flow endpoint ordered when their keys tie?

judgement.why: This asks the same empty-node-identifier question judged in P13.

precedent.topic: Whether empty node identifiers are allowed and distinguishable from flow endpoints
precedent.why: Whether an identifier field permits the empty string is an exact field constraint belonging to State 6.

topics.topic: Filesystem access available to sandboxed function code
questions: May agent code itself read and write arbitrary files inside the exchange directory and read arbitrary runtime files, or are those paths available only to the runner for loading inputs, code and outputs?

May function code inspect runtime files, its own source, directory contents or other non-input files inside the permitted mounts, or must filesystem reads be limited strictly to representations of its declared inputs?

judgement.why: This asks the same unchanged sandbox filesystem-access question judged in P2.

precedent.topic: Filesystem paths accessible to sandboxed function code
quotes:
A function node runs one admitted implementation of one contract: declared input
in, declared output out, no network, no filesystem beyond its input, no clock, no
randomness, no secret, no service handle.
precedent.why: The filesystem restriction was unchanged, and the change did not alter sandbox path access.

topics.topic: Handling of content-encoded HTTP responses
questions: If a service nevertheless returns a `Content-Encoding`, does the kernel reject it, retain the encoded bytes, or decode it before size, credential-echo and output validation checks?
Must the kernel reject a content-encoded response, decode it, or treat the encoded bytes as the body?

judgement.why: Handling HTTP content encodings is an encoding and transport-format decision belonging to State 6 or later.

topics.topic: Meaning and runtime validation role of value_schema for file ports
questions: What does it mean for file bytes or a file fixture to fit a file port's JSON `value_schema`, and is that schema validated at run and trial time or used only for edge equality?
What semantic and runtime role does `value_schema` have for a `file` port?

quotes:
A `file` port's `value_schema` is the empty schema `{}`; its fit
   is its media type (State 5, `fit_port_value`).

fit_port_value: [SCHEMA_CONSTRAINT] A file's content is never opened or inspected: the schema check of a file port compares each candidate file's media_type with the port's media_type as exactly equal text, and the size check compares each file's size_bytes with size_bound per file, never their sum.
judgement.why: The later contract fixes a file port's schema as the empty schema and defines runtime fitting solely through media type and size without inspecting content.

topics.topic: Validation and copying semantics for read-operation idempotency_key
questions: What happens when a read capability omits `idempotency_key`, supplies a non-string non-null value, or supplies text containing empty or repeated parts?
Which absent or non-string `idempotency_key` forms are accepted, and what fields are copied for a read operation?

judgement.why: Whether the manifest field is absent, null, a string or another type is a field-type and schema question belonging to State 6.

topics.topic: Whether agents may submit literal personal-data values
questions: May an agent submit raw values into a `personal_data` flow input, constant or authored trial case, even though the owner is stated to be the only reader of personal data?
May an agent submit literal personal-data values as run inputs, trial-case values or constants, or must those requests be refused because the agent would necessarily possess the value?

quotes:
A trial case is authored only by an agent with the author right, and captured
   from a failed execution only by the owner or such an agent (State 0). Either
   way it is added only when its input values fit the contract version's input
   ports, its expected outputs, when present, fit the output ports, and every
   value is within `stored_value_bytes_max` and every file within
   `trial_fixture_bytes_max` — the first failing condition in this order is
   named, ports taken in name order and, for one port, presence, carriage,
   schema, then size.

A typed literal pinned in a flow version and delivered to one input port like any
other value (K-04: a function has no configuration). Read by the run.

Candidate fields:

- `to_node`, `to_port`;
- `value`: a StoredValue (M21) of `value` carriage — a constant is never a file —
  whose class the composing agent declares with the constant.

The owner or any agent may start a run of an active version (State 0). The
   starter is recorded and never changes.

An agent never receives a `personal_data` value: wherever the surface would
   return one to an agent — run inputs and outputs, trial cases and executions,
   approval previews, trace records — it returns only the value's digest and class
   (K-14), and no `value_id`.
judgement.why: Agents may supply trial values, constants and run inputs; the personal-data restriction applies when the surface returns values to an agent.

topics.topic: Whether deterministic pseudorandomness is allowed
questions: Does the ban cover all random APIs, or only nondeterministic entropy sources?
Is deterministic pseudorandom generation allowed in a function, despite the categorical rule that a function has no randomness?

judgement.why: This asks the same deterministic-pseudorandomness question judged in P24.

precedent.topic: Whether seeded pseudorandomness is allowed in sandboxed function code
quotes:
`random.Random(seed)`
   with an explicit seed stays usable: it draws no entropy, so equal inputs
   still give equal outputs, which is what State 0's "no randomness" asks.
precedent.why: The text explicitly permits explicitly seeded deterministic pseudorandom generation and explains that the prohibition concerns entropy-based nondeterminism.

topics.topic: Which processes count against process_count
questions: Which processes count toward `process_count`: only children created by user code, the Python runner as well, or every process counted by the host user’s `RLIMIT_NPROC`?
Exactly which processes count against `process_count`?

quotes: execute_function: [BEHAVIOR] process_count bounds the tasks of the code alive at once: the runner's main thread counts as the first, every live thread and every process the code forked with os.fork counts with its threads, and bubblewrap's own processes are not counted, so process_count 1 allows code without threads or forks. Process creation other than os.fork — subprocess, os.system, os.posix_spawn, os.posix_spawnp and the os.exec family — is subprocess use and raises in the audit hook as a trap hit (A03 rule 4). The runner's audit hook, on os.fork and on starting a thread, counts the tasks of the environment's proc and, when the new task would exceed process_count, writes a resource hit to the channel and raises, so the execution concludes resource_exhausted even when the code catches the error; the parent's setrlimit, set above process_count by the tasks the runner and bubblewrap need, stays the outer bound, and a creation it refuses is reported the same way (A03 required test 2).
judgement.why: The later sandbox contract defines exactly which threads and processes count and excludes bubblewrap's own processes.

topics.topic: Which release's non-contract ceilings govern historical records and derived mapped failures
questions: How can a mapped-list oversize failure remain immutable when a later release changes `stored_value_bytes_max` and no record stores the ceiling or the derived failure?
Which release owns ceilings that are not contract fields, including request, stored-value, fixture, spool, response, text and paging ceilings, when old records and runs are used after an upgrade?
Which `stored_value_bytes_max` must readers use to derive a historical mapped-node result after an upgrade?

judgement.why: This asks the same release-ceiling ownership and historical mapped-result question judged in P14.

precedent.topic: Which release ceilings govern durable data and work across upgrades
quotes: read_value_bytes: [RETURN_SHAPE] Returns the digest-checked bytes exactly as stored.

record_change: [BEHAVIOR] MUST apply the one StoreChange given in one SQLite transaction that either writes every record the variant lists or nothing; it writes no record the variant does not list and trusts the caller for every decision of the caller's rule, checking only its own invariants: attempt numbers, unique and existing identities, existing linked records, and no edit of an immutable record. Records of the kinds that are never edited — issued contract versions, implementations, trial cases, flow versions, values, verdicts, activations and trace records — are only ever written once; for any other entity a lifecycle change — a status, who decided, resolved, revoked, cancelled or released and when, concluded_at, ended_at, waiting points, outputs — updates those fields of the entity's one record in place, and the record keeps its store position, the position of its creation; no other field of a written record ever changes.

advance_run: [SCHEMA_CONSTRAINT] A value port's PortRef names exactly one StoredValue; a mapped node's value output, once every element succeeded, is one StoredValue holding the canonical JSON array of the elements' values in element order, whose value_schema is the canonical array schema with the port's value_schema as items, of the highest class among the elements, an empty list taking the highest class among the node's inputs, the mapped list and every other input, published with put_value_bytes and written by runs when the list is first delivered, never in an element's own change; when its canonical bytes exceed the imported RELEASE_CEILING_STORED_VALUE_BYTES_MAX constant nothing is written and the node is failed for its dependants, which conclude upstream_failed, every element record staying as it is; only a list that is delivered, to a node or a flow output, is measured, and an output no edge takes fails nothing; a mapped node's file output is one SpooledFilesRef listing every element's files in element order, derived from the elements' NodeExecutions whenever it is delivered, after a restart too, since no record of its own holds it, whose disclosure_class is the highest class among the elements, an empty list taking the highest class among the node's inputs, the mapped list and every other input; a mapped element receives the list element at its map_index as its own StoredValue of the map_over port's value_schema and the list's class, or the spooled file at that position.
precedent.why: The later contracts preserve and read durable records unchanged while applying the installed release's imported ceilings whenever new work, including post-restart mapped-list derivation, is performed.

topics.topic: Acceptance and wire encoding of non-ASCII HTTP header values
questions: How are non-ASCII required-header and credential values encoded on the HTTP wire, and are they accepted at all?

topics.topic: Accepted manifest JSON shape for capabilities, instances, and required headers
questions: What exact manifest JSON shape is accepted for capabilities, instances and required headers?

topics.topic: Address fallback behavior and whether it counts as a retry
questions: When a hostname resolves to several addresses, may the client try more than one address, and is that connection fallback a retry within the attempt?

topics.topic: Application of stored_value_bytes_max to many-valued ports
questions: Is `stored_value_bytes_max` applied to the canonical bytes of the complete array, to each element separately, or to both?

topics.topic: Atomicity of mapped-output validation, storage, and delivery
questions: Can smaller aggregate outputs be stored or delivered before another aggregate output fails its size check, or must all mapped outputs be validated atomically before any delivery?

topics.topic: Classification of HTTP status codes outside 100–599
questions: How is a syntactically parseable status code outside 100–599 classified?

topics.topic: Credential newline trimming and control-character definition
questions: Does trailing newline removal recognize LF only or CRLF, and which Unicode or ASCII code points count as controls?

topics.topic: Definition of an earlier implementation eligible for rollback
questions: What makes an implementation eligible as `earlier`: submission order, prior activation order, or merely being non-current?

topics.topic: Detecting resource-limit violations caught by user code
questions: How can the kernel determine that memory, process or scratch limits were hit when user code catches the resulting `MemoryError`, `OSError` or allocation failure and returns a conforming result?

topics.topic: Deterministic precedence among multiple operation-output validation failures
questions: When several output members are missing, invalid or oversized, which port determines the recorded failure detail and first named reason?

topics.topic: Disclosure-class computation for cyclic graphs and reliance on earlier validation phases
questions: How is the reachable disclosure class computed for a graph containing a cycle when phase 8 is reached after phase 7 has already found no cycle, and more generally is disclosure computation permitted to rely on the earlier phase having passed?

topics.topic: Equality semantics for JSON guard values
questions: What equality relation is used for JSON guard values, especially numbers such as `1` and `1.0` and booleans such as `true` versus `1`?

topics.topic: Exact trace window included in the repair view
questions: What exact trace window does the repair view return?

topics.topic: Identity semantics for NodeExecution records
questions: Is a NodeExecution a value identified by all its facts, or an entity identified by its attempt coordinates?

topics.topic: Index base and comparison rule for mapped elements
questions: Are map indices zero-based list indices compared numerically?

topics.topic: Interaction of array schemas and many cardinality in query serialization
questions: How do schema type `array` and port cardinality `many` combine for query serialization, and are nested lists or a cardinality-`many` port with an array element schema valid?

topics.topic: MCP transport, envelope, token placement, and request-size boundary
questions: Which MCP transport and message envelope are used, which bytes count toward the request limit, and where in that envelope is the token carried?

topics.topic: Meaning of an explicitly empty trial-case selection
questions: Does an explicitly supplied empty case list mean ‘all cases’, ‘execute zero cases’, or an invalid request distinct from omission of the field?

topics.topic: Ordering of pinned-digest comparison during proposed-binding acceptance
questions: Where in rule 5’s ordered checks is comparison of the current operation digest with the proposal’s pinned digest performed, especially when both the digest and another record or instance condition have changed?

topics.topic: Outcome for an incomplete HTTP response body after final headers
questions: Which outcome applies when a final status line and headers arrive but the response body does not complete?

topics.topic: Outcome precedence when sandbox cleanup is unconfirmed
questions: When cleanup is unconfirmed after a timeout, resource limit or sandbox trap, which outcome must be recorded?

topics.topic: Outcome when an outbound request cannot be constructed or sent due to size
questions: What happens when a valid invocation produces an outbound request too large for the HTTP client, operating system or service transport to construct or send, before the first byte is written?

topics.topic: Output-size checking when a result cannot be canonically serialized
questions: How is output size determined before contract validation when the returned object has extra keys, non-JSON objects, cycles, invalid numbers or another form that cannot be canonically serialized?

topics.topic: Re-admission and rollback validity across sandbox releases
questions: After the sandbox interpreter, trapped APIs or dependencies change in a new release, may an old verdict still be reused and an old implementation rolled back without re-admission?

topics.topic: Required HTTP protocol version, framing, and wire header representation
questions: Which HTTP protocol version and framing are required, given that HTTP/2 uses pseudo-headers and may not send the specified `Host` and header representation?

topics.topic: Required carriage and cardinality for path-placeholder input ports
questions: Must a placeholder input also have `value` carriage and cardinality `one`, or may a `file` or `many` port pass proposal validation and then fail every invocation’s pre-send check?

topics.topic: Text-length bounds for manifest and required-header fields
questions: What bounds apply to service IDs, operation names, paths, base URLs, required-header names and values, and other manifest text before they are stored, included in previews or sent?

topics.topic: Tie-breaking order for edges or constants with equal stated sort keys
questions: How are edges or constants ordered when the stated sort keys are equal but their remaining content differs?

topics.topic: Unit used to measure redacted failure-detail length
questions: Is the reported failure-detail length measured in UTF-8 bytes, Unicode code points, or characters after replacement and truncation?

topics.topic: Whether a StandingGrant may target a function node
questions: Can a StandingGrant be created for a function node?

topics.topic: Whether caller-supplied identities are refused only for created records or also for references
questions: Does this refusal apply only when a caller supplies the identity of the record being created, or also when an identity is supplied as a reference to an existing record?

topics.topic: Whether configured secret and internal-store paths may contain symlinked parent directories
questions: May any parent directory component of a configured secret path or an internal store path be a symbolic link?

topics.topic: Whether credential and token non-disclosure is provenance-based or byte-sequence-based
questions: Are these prohibitions about secret provenance or about matching byte sequences? If they are byte-sequence prohibitions, what happens when an owner or agent submits a value equal to a token or credential, or a service returns it somewhere other than the scanned response body?

topics.topic: Whether flow reachability accounts for mutually incompatible guards
questions: Is reachability purely structural over all guarded edges, or must the proof account for guard values and reject paths whose combined guard conditions can never be enabled?

topics.topic: Whether operation outputs may lower the disclosure class of their inputs
questions: Can an operation that receives `personal_data` return an output declared `open`, thereby lowering the class, or must the output be raised to at least the highest actual or reachable input class?

topics.topic: Whether the bubblewrap version and behavior must be release-pinned
questions: Is any probe-passing bubblewrap version accepted, or must its version and required behavior be pinned by the release?
